source.title: Reconciling Modern Deep Learning with Traditional Optimization Analyses: The Intrinsic Learning Rate
source.authors: Zhiyuan Li; Kaifeng Lyu; Sanjeev Arora

record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for networks trained with gradient methods from initialization, bearing on V1, though the experiments focus on intrinsic learning rate and equilibrium.
record.gate_note: The study reports training accuracy on CIFAR and explicitly says PreResNet32 reaches 100% training accuracy on a 1,000-image CIFAR-10 subset but cannot sustain it. Other reported training-accuracy comparisons are described as similar or shown only in figures; no cited prior-work results are included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training classification accuracy for convolutional networks on CIFAR, bearing on V1 through gradient-based training under normalization and weight-decay schedules. It is not an original source for V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct, but equilibrium and its inverse-intrinsic-LR timescale are experimentally supported conjectures, not general established results. The authors develop a scale-invariant SGD-plus-BN-plus-weight-decay framework, identify intrinsic LR as LR times weight decay, and report instability near zero loss under full-batch GD with weight decay. They also find that small initial learning rates can achieve comparable generalization with longer training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-based training from initialized networks and reports classification training accuracy, but focuses on batch normalization, weight decay, intrinsic learning rate and equilibrium rather than systematically testing model size or zero training error across benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Training behavior and equilibrium depend on learning-rate and weight-decay schedules; the authors also report instability near zero loss with full-batch GD and weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-rate times weight decay controls the observed equilibrium, with recovery time approximately inverse in that product.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested normalized networks, intrinsic learning rate controls function-space equilibrium and the time needed to reach it.

fits_no_version.finding: Large initial intrinsic learning rates improve robustness to extreme initialization scales within the training budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For BN-equipped PreResNet32, initialization scale and the initial LR/weight-decay schedule jointly affect training speed.

record.problems: The explicit perfect-training-accuracy result is for a subsampled dataset of 1,000 CIFAR-10 images and is transient. Most other training-accuracy results are plotted without exact values in the text; no uncertainty estimates are stated for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No other relevant numerical training-accuracy results were stated outside the included rows. Figure 3 and Figure 10 discuss test performance and small learning rates without a textual training-error result; exact plotted training-accuracy values are figure-only and were not expanded into additional schedule-specific rows.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, systematic capacity comparisons, Adam, and systematic comparisons of early stopping or regularization recipes. Full-dataset near-zero training error cannot be determined from the supplied figure text.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth with and without identity shortcuts, and the specified plain-network or Fixup alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient preservation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth in plain networks.
Learning rates relative to the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction during recovery, and sharpness tracking the stability threshold.
Accuracy gain or learning-rate tolerance compared with otherwise matching networks without BN, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Failure to sustain perfect interpolation does not independently limit V1, which asserts attainment rather than persistence. No additional verdict follows from schedule agreement alone. The supplied text contains figure labels and axes but insufficient curve information to assign absolute training-error outcomes to R2–R7. Figures 3 and 10 were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100 training error in the stated experiment results, random or corrupted labels, smaller model capacity, early stopping, or regularized recipes as a systematic comparison.

rows.subject: PreResNet32
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with weight decay on a subsampled CIFAR-10 dataset.
rows.value: 100% training accuracy, but unable to stay long; oscillates between zero loss and high loss
rows.note: Authors explicitly report the model can reach 100% training accuracy but cannot persistently maintain perfect interpolation under this recipe.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report reaching 100% training accuracy. V1 says reaches, so failure to maintain that accuracy does not make attainment partial. The oscillation applies to the BN-plus-weight-decay phase; weight decay is removed at epoch 30000. Full-batch GD and the 1000-image subset narrow the evidence relative to V1's SGD/Adam benchmark setting.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Figure 1 caption, lines 256–260; oscillation explained in the preceding Section 4 paragraph.

rows.subject: PreResNet32
rows.operation_detail: SGD training under five random learning-rate/weight-decay schedules, then shared settings after epoch 500.
rows.note: Text says the schedules exhibit similar test/train accuracy after switching to the same intrinsic learning rate; exact training-accuracy values are only plotted.
rows.check: Similar accuracy across schedules does not establish near-zero training error. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve values. Record separately the equilibrium phase and the phase after LR reduction and weight-decay removal at epoch 1000.

rows.subject: PreResNet32
rows.operation_detail: SGD training with matched sequences of intrinsic learning rates using either learning-rate decay or weight-decay decay.
rows.note: The text says the two networks share almost the same effective learning rate and train/test accuracy for most of the time; the plotted accuracy values are not stated.
rows.check: Agreement between the two schedules does not establish near-zero training error. The supplied text lacks readable curve values. The row also omits weight-decay removal and tenfold LR reduction at epoch 8000.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: BN and SGD training at different intrinsic learning rates, followed by learning-rate and weight-decay changes that preserve their product.
rows.note: Training accuracy is plotted, but the text reports the equilibrium-time relationship rather than explicit training-accuracy results.
rows.check: Training accuracy is relevant, but its values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. Equilibrium recovery time does not itself establish near-zero training error.
